title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an insider misuse case, not a model failure. A person with legitimate access to law enforcement systems is accused of querying them for a purpose the access was never granted for. The systems named are a camera network, a tag reader system, and a state criminal justice database, all built and provisioned for police work, and the alleged misuse sits entirely inside that authorised access rather than in any defect in the tools.

The failure is one of purpose, and it is the hardest kind to catch at the point of use. Each individual query would have looked ordinary to the system, because the account and the credentials were valid. What would have been needed is a check outside the query itself, such as review of who searched for whom and why, or a limit on searches that have no case attached. The reporting does not say whether any such logging or review existed.

What is not established is guilt. The eight counts are charges returned by a grand jury, and an indictment is an accusation, not a finding. The account of the tracking itself comes from investigators and from a complainant speaking anonymously, and no verdict or admission is reported.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff’s deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, was released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violation of oath by a public officer, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Investigators say he misused the sheriff’s office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons between April and May 2024. He was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman he is accused of tracking spoke anonymously, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
